ryans.name: Ryan Blaney
ryans.title: NASCAR Cup Series driver for Team Penske
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Blaney** (born December 31, 1993) is an American stock car racing driver who drives the No. 12 Ford Mustang Dark Horse for Team Penske in the NASCAR Cup Series [1][2]. He won the NASCAR Cup Series championship in 2023 [2][5]. Team Penske lists his birthplace as Hartford, Ohio, and his residence as Mooresville, North Carolina [2].

ryans.name: Ryan Craig
ryans.title: Head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Craig** (born January 6, 1982) is a Canadian ice hockey coach and former centre who is head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights of the NHL [1][3]. He was named the franchise's fifth head coach on June 17, 2026, replacing John Tortorella [1][2]. He was an assistant on the Vegas staff that won the Stanley Cup in 2023 [1].
known_for: Fifth head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights
2016 Calder Cup as Lake Erie captain

ryans.name: Ryan Day
ryans.title: Head football coach at The Ohio State University
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Patrick Day** (born March 12, 1979) is an American college and professional football coach and former collegiate quarterback who serves as the head football coach at The Ohio State University [1][2][4]. Named to succeed Urban Meyer on December 4, 2018, after going 3–0 as acting head coach at the start of the 2018 season, Day officially took over as Ohio State's head coach on January 2, 2019 [1][2][3].
known_for: Head football coach at Ohio State University (2019–present)
Winning the 2024 College Football Playoff National Championship
2019 Big Ten Coach of the Year and five CFP appearances
Childhood and adolescent mental health advocacy with On Our Sleeves

ryans.name: Ryan Garcia
ryans.title: American professional boxer
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Garcia** (born 1998) is an American professional boxer from Victorville, California [6]. Nicknamed "King Ry," he has held the World Boxing Council (WBC) welterweight title since February 2026 [5][6][7]. He previously won the WBC interim lightweight title in 2021 [1][2].

ryans.name: Ryan Giggs
ryans.title: Welsh former footballer and manager
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Joseph Giggs** (born 29 November 1973) is a Welsh former professional footballer and coach [1][2]. He spent his entire club playing career at Manchester United (1990–2014), making 963 appearances and winning 13 Premier League titles and two UEFA Champions League titles [2][3]. He later managed the Wales national team from 2018 until resigning in June 2022 [4][5].

ryans.name: Matt Ryan
ryans.title: Former NFL quarterback; Falcons President of Football
ryans.lead_summary: **Matthew Thomas Ryan** (born May 17, 1985) is an American football executive and former NFL quarterback [1][2]. Nicknamed "Matty Ice," he spent most of his playing career with the Atlanta Falcons, won Associated Press NFL Most Valuable Player honors in 2016, and in January 2026 was named the Falcons’ President of Football [2][3].

ryans.name: Nolan Ryan
ryans.title: Hall of Fame MLB pitcher
ryans.lead_summary: **Lynn Nolan Ryan Jr.** (born January 31, 1947) is an American former Major League Baseball pitcher nicknamed the "Ryan Express" [1][2]. Over a record-tying 27 seasons he pitched for the New York Mets, California Angels, Houston Astros, and Texas Rangers [1][2]. He holds the major-league career records for strikeouts (5,714) and no-hitters (seven) and was elected to the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1999 [1][2][3][4].

ryans.name: Ryan Shazier
ryans.title: Former Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker; author and Steelers offensive assistant
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Dean Shazier** (born 1991 or 1992) is an American former professional football linebacker, author and coach [11][13]. He played college football at Ohio State and was the Pittsburgh Steelers' first-round pick, 15th overall, in the 2014 NFL draft [3][9]. He was selected to two Pro Bowls [11]. On December 4, 2017, he suffered a spinal cord injury while making a tackle against the Cincinnati Bengals. He had spinal stabilization surgery and never played again [4][5][9].
known_for: Two-time Pro Bowl linebacker for the Pittsburgh Steelers
Recovery from a 2017 spinal cord injury
